text:
Clayton Keller, Utah's captain, is having one of the best playmaking starts in the league: 29 points in 23 games, 24 of them assists, and 19 on the power play. He's playing almost 21 minutes a night over his last ten games, more than two minutes above his season pace, and our numbers project him for close to 98 points.

The goals lag. He has 5 on chances worth about 7.7, shooting 8.5% against a usual 12 to 13 for forwards, and only one in his last ten games. That gap tends to close; he keeps getting to the net.

Not everything is rosy. Utah gets a slim edge in expected goals at five on five with him on but does clearly better without him, about nine points better by share, a big gap for a top-line player. Evolving-Hockey had him sixth among forwards in wins above replacement last season, while noting some of it came from hot shooting. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking had him in the 98th percentile for primary shot assists, so the passing is who he is. Utah has won only three of its last ten games with him; the goals would help.
headline: Keller is feeding everyone in Utah
